rounds.text: Nihar Info Global Ltd is currently trading at a significant discount, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.72x [E2] and a P/E of 7x [E1], both of which sit well below their respective sector benchmarks of 2.13x and 21x [E6, E7]. This valuation disconnect is underscored by a discounted cash flow analysis suggesting an intrinsic value of Rs 27 per share, providing a substantial margin of safety of 82.8% [E38, E39]. The company has demonstrated explosive growth, with compounded sales growth of 181% and profit growth of 119% over the trailing twelve months [E15, E17]. Furthermore, the completion of capital expenditure projects, evidenced by the 100% reduction in capital work in progress, suggests that new capacity is coming online to support future operations [E35]. The company is also benefiting from a sector tailwind in Information Technology, which provides a favorable macro backdrop for its business model [E58, E59]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with negative operating cash flow [E28, E29], a lack of dividend payments [E4], and a history of poor share price performance [E18, E19, E20, E21].

Conceded: [E38] and [E39]. Despite theoretical margin of safety arguments, the company suffers from severe cash flow erosion, posting a negative operating cash flow of Rs -2.12 Cr and a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -3.07x against reported profit in Mar 2026 [E28, E29]. This fundamental disconnect is compounded by a dismal long-term share price performance, reflecting negative growth over 1, 3, 5, and 10-year horizons [E18, E19, E20, E21], sitting at the absolute bottom of its 52-week range [E5]. Furthermore, structural quality is heavily undermined by low promoter backing at 27.5% with nearly 27% of those holdings pledged [E46, E49], high debtor days stretching to 180 [E50], and risks of interest capitalization [E48]. Operating margins remain weak and inconsistent at just 4% [E24, E26], while historical profitability has been dismal with a 3-year median ROE of -26% [E22, E47].

Conceded: [E28] and [E29]. While operating cash flow was negative in Mar 2026, the company's fundamental growth trajectory shows massive acceleration with 3-year compounded sales growth at 60% and trailing twelve-month sales growth reaching 181% [E14, E15]. Profit growth is similarly explosive, up 97% over 3 years and 119% over the trailing twelve months [E16, E17], alongside expanding quarterly operating margins that rebounded by 82 percentage points year-over-year [E25]. The market price ignores this massive fundamental acceleration, trading at a steep discount with a P/E of just 7x against a sector benchmark of 21x [E1, E6] and a price-to-book ratio of 0.72x against a sector benchmark of 2.13x [E2, E7]. Furthermore, working capital efficiency has dramatically improved, with requirements dropping sharply from 133 days to 67.9 days [E45], and completed capital expenditure means new capacity is coming online [E35]. Operating in an Information Technology sector tailwind [E58], the company trades at a massive valuation disconnect given a reverse DCF showing today's price implies an unjustifiably pessimistic -7.7% earnings growth [E40].

Conceded: [E14, E15, E16, E17]. While the bull highlights explosive growth, this performance is disconnected from cash generation, as evidenced by a negative operating cash flow of Rs -2.12 Cr and a cash conversion ratio of -3.07x in Mar 2026 [E28, E29]. The bull’s reliance on margin expansion [E25] ignores the broader reality of an inconsistent operating-margin trend over the last three years [E26, E27] and a long-term decline in operating margins from 6% to 4% [E24]. Furthermore, the bull’s optimism regarding valuation [E1, E2, E6, E7] fails to account for the significant risks of a low 27.5% promoter holding [E46] and the fact that 26.9% of those promoter holdings are pledged [E49]. The company’s financial health is further undermined by high debtors of 180 days [E50] and the potential capitalization of interest costs [E48]. Finally, the bull’s focus on growth ignores the persistent negative share price performance, which has compounded at -23% over the last year and -11% over the last decade [E18, E21].
